speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 98.5°F (36.9°C), Blood Pressure 137/88 mmHg, Heart Rate 90/min, Respiratory Rate 12/min, Oxygen Saturation 98% on room air. Appearance: Obese patient with facial hirsutism. Lower Extremity Exam: Inspection shows no visible abnormalities, erythema, or swelling. Palpation reveals tenderness over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. Range of Motion is full without significant pain or limitation. Special Tests are negative for ligamentous instability. X-Ray Knee findings: No fracture, dislocation, or appreciable joint effusion. MRI Knee: Optional if clinical suspicion persists despite negative initial workup.

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints)

The location you describe—medial aspect of the tibia inferior to the patella—is classic for shin splints, especially with recent increased activity. Please ignore the previous suggestion of pneumonia, as your symptoms do not align with a respiratory infection. I will now request a focused physical exam to check for tenderness and rule out a stress fracture.
